Salento retains its colonial streets and is closely connected to Colombia's coffee culture. On a walk through town, you can visit artisan workshops and stop for a cup of local coffee. The town reveals everyday life in the coffee region, where nature excursions go hand in hand with craft workshops and small cafés.

Its proximity to the Cocora Valley makes Salento a convenient stop on a trip to see the wax palms. After walking forest and mountain trails, visitors return here to explore its streets and sample local cuisine. Viewpoints offer vistas of the surrounding landscape, while the story of coffee connects the town to the region's plantations.

The Salobra River is visited alongside other natural bodies of water around Bom Jardim. The main activity here is snorkeling in clear water.

During the water excursion, visitors watch fish and plants. A visit to the Salobra is combined with a walk to natural pools and a trip to the Enchanted Aquarium; the exact order depends on the selected itinerary.

Salta is one of the most vibrant resort cities in northwestern Argentina. Beneath the canopies of exotic trees, it hides places of striking natural beauty. Founded in 1582, the city carries its history in the walls of old buildings, many of which have become cultural heritage landmarks. You can visit the San Francisco Cathedral and see statues of the Virgin Mary and Christ. According to local tradition, these statues can heal illnesses.

From Salta, you can take the legendary Train to the Clouds to San Antonio de los Cobres, a town tucked away in the Andes at an altitude of 4220 meters, and admire a landscape carved by deep canyons. Before leaving Salta, make time to see the Hill of Seven Colors shimmering in the sunlight.

Salta also offers tastings of aromatic wines from local producers, accompanied by the region's famous flavorful beef. In the evening, be sure to experience one of Argentina's most celebrated spectacles: tango.
